frames.narration: The screen needs the customer's name, the last 3 orders and the items in each. First, the REST way: one request per resource.
Both answers come back with every field of the user and every field of each order, although the screen uses only a few.
The app only now learns the order ids, so it needs a second round of requests, one per order, to get the items.
REST needed 5 requests in 2 rounds. On a slow mobile network each round costs a lot of time.
GraphQL: the app sends one query that names the user's name, the orders and the item names, nothing else.

messages.label: query { user { name orders { items { name } } } }

frames.narration: The API collects the data from the backend services itself, which sit close to it on a fast network.
One response arrives with exactly the requested fields. One round trip and no unused data. gRPC would send compact binary messages, which suits calls between your own services.
